g.text: HELP / GET STARTED
01 / START HERE
timemachine init is setup, not a backup. Save a checkpoint or wrap a session.
In your project terminal: timemachine run -- YOUR_COMMAND
Replace YOUR_COMMAND with any executable and its arguments.
Example: timemachine run -- python -c 'print(123)'
Files are saved before and after the command; no AI agent is required.
To save manually: timemachine checkpoint -m 'Before my changes'
02 / INSPECT
1 History / 2 Files / 3 Diff Tab moves focus
a switches Simple / Advanced; t switches dark / light.
Arrows or j/k navigate; Enter/d opens the selected file.
/ filters loaded archive entries; Load older fetches the next page.
f filters paths. Find searches this preview; Enter/n cycles matches.
v toggles saved file/diff. b sets a saved comparison origin.
03 / RECOVER DELIBERATELY
u reviews Undo; Ctrl+R reviews Redo; the primary button follows session order.
r reviews the selected full checkpoint. s restores only the selected file/path.
Every review checks current files, then freezes and revalidates the intent.
Cancel is always the default. Newer conflicts refuse writes.
F5 refresh / t light-dark / Esc archive or cancel / q quit
No animation, sound, daemon or automatic restore.
SCOPE / Selected local bytes, modes, directories and opaque symlinks.
Excluded trees and Git history/index are not restored. Ignored files can
contain secrets. Stop external writers; recovery is not globally atomic.
For interruption/corruption: preserve the store and run timemachine doctor.
CLI alternative: timemachine --plain history; timemachine undo --preview --json
Return
